hypothesis_loop.selection_reason: B08 Finland heat pumps generated COHORT_READY_SHOCK_ACTIVATION: an ageing installed cohort may remain latent until a climate/performance shock causes owners to transact. Australian residential pools were selected as an unrelated high-load seasonal asset with a mature installed base, pumps/chlorinators/controllers, deep parts markets and measurable replacement data.
hypothesis_loop.hypothesis: Australian hot-season/high-use periods should activate latent failures/replacements in ageing pool pumps, chlorinators and controllers, while routine maintenance is commoditized; the stronger commercial cell should be model-specific diagnosis and rapid repair/replacement.
falsifiers: No evidence links seasonal high use or heat to equipment demand/failure.
Pool equipment is standardized enough that model-specific compatibility adds little.
Routine and complex repairs are both already fully commoditized.
Owners overwhelmingly stay inside existing pool-service relationships, leaving little independent search/routing.

exact_analysis_questions.how_much_more_for_convenience_certainty_: No revealed WTP. Waterworks charges the same A$135 ex-GST labour line for callout, pump overhaul and many equipment replacements, suggesting diagnosis/fit rather than travel alone drives complexity. No clean urgent/summer premium was found.
exact_analysis_questions.which_problem_states_show_strongest_econ: Ageing 5–10+ year pump with failed seal/bearing/motor; old single-speed pump where a high-efficiency variable-speed replacement materially reduces operating cost; generation-specific Astral CTX parts where an apparently correct part will not fit another production generation.
exact_analysis_questions.current_options: Pool shops/service companies, OEM-authorized dealers, general pool technicians, licensed electricians where required, specialist parts ecommerce, repair workshops.
exact_analysis_questions.is_there_room_for_us: Not in generic maintenance or parts. Better wedge: photo/data-plate model-generation identification + repair-vs-replace + energy-cost comparison + correctly specified replacement.
exact_analysis_questions.best_gtm: model + fault queries; 'old vs new style' parts queries; repair-vs-variable-speed-upgrade calculator; summer readiness checks; pool-equipment passport; local licensed repair routing.
exact_analysis_questions.same_pattern_other_country: B08 Finland supported cohort readiness plus cold-weather activation. Australia pools clearly have seasonal runtime and replacement cohorts, but direct hard data linking heatwaves to equipment failure is missing. Therefore shock activation does not replicate yet.
exact_analysis_questions.why_country_difference: Pool pumps are continuously maintainable and many owners already have service relationships. Hot weather strongly raises chemistry and runtime load, but a pool-pump failure is less existential than a heating failure in Finland, which may weaken measurable shock urgency.
exact_analysis_questions.what_does_it_reveal_about_country: Australia has enough pool penetration to justify national equipment regulation and a public model-level energy database. The market is mature enough that efficiency—not just mechanical failure—can drive replacement economics.
exact_analysis_questions.macro_pattern: An asset can have both a mechanical replacement clock and an operating-cost obsolescence clock. For pools, the energy clock is unusually measurable because pumps are a large household load and are now regulated/labeled.
exact_analysis_questions.falsifier_result: Core replacement/compatibility thesis supported. The specific B08 climate-shock-to-hardware-failure transfer is unresolved and should be treated as failed-to-replicate, not assumed.

mechanism_candidates.statement: A single homeowner system contains nested components with materially different warranty/wear clocks, so the economically relevant aftermarket is a graph of sub-assets rather than one asset lifecycle.
mechanism_candidates.observed_examples: 1-year sensors/seals/wear parts; 2–3-year pumps/chlorinators/controllers; 5-year compressors; up to 25-year heat exchangers.
mechanism_candidates.next_replication_test: Test another multi-component installed system such as domestic water treatment, boiler plant or smart-home energy stack.

mechanism_candidates.statement: A functioning installed asset can become economically obsolete before mechanical failure when a successor has a large, measurable operating-cost advantage.
mechanism_candidates.observed_statistic: Government guidance: 5-star variable-speed pump uses 55% less energy than a 1-star single-speed pump.
mechanism_candidates.next_replication_test: Test boilers, ventilation fans, refrigeration or pumps where energy-label changes create upgrade economics.

mechanism_candidates.statement: In urgent/technical replacement markets, installer or specialist-shop advice can control successor choice more strongly than consumer independent comparison.
mechanism_candidates.observed_statistic: 62% of surveyed Australian like-for-like replacers cited installer/pool-shop advice.
mechanism_candidates.next_replication_test: Look for measured advisor influence in heat pumps, stairlifts, boilers or EV charging.

MC-COHORT_READY_SHOCK_ACTIVATION.new_learning: B09 verifies higher summer duty cycle and hot-weather chemistry stress, but no sufficiently hard failure/repair-volume series was found. Do not promote climate shock activation from operational load alone.

LEGACY_INTERFACE_LOCK_IN.new_evidence: 2016 Australian survey: among like-for-like replacements, 32% cited size/space and 22% existing piping; CTX components also fork by production generation.

MC-MULTI_CLOCK_AFTERMARKET_TRIGGER.new_learning: Pool pumps add mechanical-age, component-warranty, energy-cost and product-efficiency clocks, but the hypothesized heatwave failure clock remains unproven.

next_probe.sector: remote cabin water/frost/climate monitoring and remediation
next_probe.selection_reason: B09 failed to replicate COHORT_READY_SHOCK_ACTIVATION because direct climate-to-hardware-failure evidence was weak. Norwegian cabins are a better causal test: remote properties, freezing conditions, water damage, insurer loss data, and large cabin stock allow us to test whether weather shocks create directly measured economic losses and whether monitoring/prevention can capture value.
next_probe.hypothesis: In remote properties, weather shocks create outsized loss because failures remain undetected. The strongest intermediary/ecommerce opportunity should therefore shift upstream from repair to prevention: sensing, automatic shutoff, frost/power monitoring and verified local response.
falsifiers: No quantified cabin water/frost loss data exists.
Insurance already mandates/provides monitoring so the commercial wedge is closed.
Connectivity/power constraints make remote monitoring unreliable.
Integrated Norwegian smart-home/cabin providers already dominate the prevention stack.
Monitoring savings are too small relative to hardware/install cost.
